chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami and Kulayb Al-Asadi has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Abdur Rahman Al-Asam, from Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad Al-Hadrami and Kulayb Al-Asadi.

key_terms.أَبِي بَكْرٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ: Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, a key narrator
key_terms.الْأَصَمِّ: Al-Asam, a narrator's epithet meaning 'the deaf' or 'the mute'
key_terms.حَضْرَمِيِّ: Al-Hadrami, indicating lineage or origin from Hadramawt
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him (honorific for the father)
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a major narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami and Kulayb Al-Asadi verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the specific isnad for narrations attributed to Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Kulayb al-Asadi, tracing them back to his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (ra), via a chain of prominent Kufi and Basran scholars. This explicit linkage to the Ahl al-Bayt underscores the reliability of these companions as transmitters and highlights the scholarly rigor employed in distinguishing authentic reports within the hadith corpus.
